fact: A contributed article in Seychelles Nation states that the Civil Status records were computerised in 1989 and that two sets of records are currently kept, a manual record under the Civil Status Act and a computerised record for the National Population Database, which is updated daily from occurrences registered by the Civil Status; it speaks of vital events and vital records without listing births and deaths separately.

The article states that the Civil Status Division in the Ministry of Employment, Immigration and Civil Status, with the National Bureau of Statistics, is the agency responsible for the civil registration and vital statistics system, each under its own law.

The Civil Status (Amendment) Act 2021, assented to on 4 November 2021 and commencing on a date the Minister appoints by Gazette notice, makes it the duty of the Chief Officer of Civil Status to maintain the registers of births, stillbirths and deaths, and has a death declared at a civil status office; the Act does not say the registers in use are kept digitally.

fact: The Civil Status Act as in force on 1 November 2022 makes the Chief Officer of Civil Status, appointed by the President and answering to the Minister responsible for civil status, keeper of the registers of births and deaths, with a Central Civil Status Office in Victoria and offices at Praslin, La Digue and Anse Royale; section 107A, inserted by Act 45 of 2021, lets him accept statements, forms and signatures through an electronic medium, while the registers themselves are prescribed as numbered pages kept in duplicate.
